title: Partnership and LLC accounting
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 4 guide matches, 23 question matches, 15 assessment matches, and 35 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: Are book capital, section 704(b) capital, tax-basis capital, and outside basis distinct?
questions.finding: Tax measures remain distinct: §743(b) creates transferee-only partnership-property basis and tax-item adjustments; it does not change common inside basis or the transferee’s capital account. That answers the tax-basis distinction, not GAAP equity presentation.
questions.remaining_gap: Current US GAAP partnership presentation and partner-specific ledger/liability facts remain open.

questions.question: How do cash/noncash contributions and built-in gain/loss affect capital and later allocations?
questions.finding: A’s contributed property carries a $6,000 initial built-in gain; after first-year tax depreciation, a $9,000 year-two sale sends $5,400 gain to A. If AB then liquidates with $19,000 cash, A has $9,400 basis and $100 gain while B has $9,600 basis and $100 loss.
questions.remaining_gap: The example is tax regulation, not client facts or a GAAP capital-account policy; agreement method choice and special 704(c) rules remain.

questions.question: How are profits/losses allocated and midyear admissions/exits handled?
questions.finding: Prior sources still describe agreement-based allocations and varying-interest rules; this pass adds no new midyear-admission or safe-harbor evidence.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual allocations, admission/exit dates, agreement and applicable tax-year elections remain entity-specific.

questions.question: How do distributions, withdrawals, liability relief, and service payments affect partners?
questions.finding: General tax routes distinguish §734(b) common-basis adjustment from §743(b) transferee-only basis; §736 classifies full-interest retirement payments and §736(b)(2)-(3) has conditional receivables/goodwill scope.
questions.remaining_gap: Complex noncash/liability distributions and service payments require the actual facts, agreement, partner/entity status and current-year tax law.

questions.question: How are transfers, retirement, liquidation and windup represented?
questions.finding: General tax mechanics now separate a third-party transfer from partnership liquidation payments, distinguish §736(a) from §736(b), and reconcile final distributions to outside basis; the proposed windup schedule keeps tax and book measures separate.
questions.remaining_gap: The question also asks how windup is represented: US GAAP presentation, legal transfer/windup rights, member status, and agreement-specific allocation/payment terms remain unresolved.

recommended_additions: Add a dedicated role- and accounting-basis-specific guide using the scope and reconciliations in the brief.
Add a worked 704(c) multiyear schedule ending in liquidation, with outside-basis and §731/§732 reconciliation.
Add conditional §736 treatment and §734/§743 election/mandatory-trigger distinctions; keep GAAP equity and agreement rights separate.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
Current Codification wording and entity-specific application remain to be checked; this follow-up does not infer that current ASC verification requires paid access.
priority_rationale: Partnership structures are common across investment, real-estate, operating and family-office entities; book capital, tax capital and outside basis are commonly conflated.

title: Fund accounting and investment partnerships
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 10 guide matches, 31 question matches, 32 assessment matches, and 59 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: How should a US fund close distinguish portfolio assets/NAV, investor capital, manager/GP, and portfolio-company books?
questions.finding: Prior ASC 946 and custody materials already distinguish fund assets/NAV and investor capital from GP/manager and portfolio-company reporting; this pass reinforces the boundary but adds no new consolidation evidence.
questions.remaining_gap: ASC 810 and legal title/control require the actual structure, contracts, and ledger.

questions.question: What valuation evidence supports private investment fair value and NAV?
questions.finding: BDO’s 2018 discussion of a working draft adds a general calibration and security-class method framework, but current authoritative security-class guidance is unverified and entity-specific value remains open.
questions.remaining_gap: The source is a nonauthoritative 2018 discussion of an AICPA working draft; current authoritative security-class guidance, actual class rights, transaction orderliness, measurement-date inputs and professional valuation remain unverified; IPEV remains excluded.

questions.question: How should commitments, capital calls, distributions and unfunded commitments reconcile?
questions.finding: Prior ILPA notice examples and IRS tax reporting sources already provide the general call/distribution/unfunded commitment reconciliation scope.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual commitment terms, call types, subsequent changes and unusual distributions remain agreement-dependent.

questions.question: How do carried-interest fees versus profit allocations affect fund, GP, and manager statements?
questions.finding: Fund class allocation and manager carry revenue are separate questions. FASB staff’s 2020 view is that service-compensation carry is within Topic 606 regardless of cash/equity form; KPMG’s 2025 interpretation of the 2016 TRG/SEC Observer comments allows a consistent ownership model on specific facts with full ASC 810/323 analysis. Ares used ASC 323 for carry and ASC 606 for incentive fees in 2018.
questions.remaining_gap: Not a universal policy choice or Board-level conclusion. Reporting-entity structure, contract substance, variable-consideration reversal, clawback, consolidation/equity-method facts and current Codification remain necessary.

questions.question: How do custody, investor delivery, and regulatory audit duties interact?
questions.finding: Custody, audit, investor delivery and adviser obligations remain a separate regulatory analysis from fund accounting.
questions.remaining_gap: Current adviser and pool status, custody, audit exception, delivery dates, Form PF/CFTC/ERISA facts and later legal developments require current review.

questions.question: How should ASC 946 fund financial statements present net assets, class NAV/capital activity, subscriptions, and realized/unrealized performance?
questions.finding: Prior ASC 946 technical material already supports the general fund financial-statement and class-capital presentation path.
questions.remaining_gap: Registered-fund requirements and applicable statement set depend on fund status and reporting facts; current Codification review remains.

questions.question: How are management fees, fee waivers, expense limitations, and offsets presented in an ASC 946 fund?
questions.finding: Fund management-fee expense/waiver/offset accounting is distinct from the manager’s contract revenue. The new manager-side evidence treats separate management services under Topic 606 while analyzing carried interest independently as service compensation or a possible equity ownership arrangement.
questions.remaining_gap: Fund fee terms, waiver/expense-cap mechanics, offsets, consolidation, manager contract and ledger remain unreviewed.

questions.question: How should contractual waterfall distributions sequence return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carry and clawback?
questions.finding: Prior ILPA model LPA shows one waterfall sequence and bracketed alternatives; it remains an illustration, not a universal distribution rule.
questions.remaining_gap: No actual waterfall, side letters, preferred-return basis, clawback or realized/unrealized ledger was inspected.

questions.question: How do hedge high-water marks, classes/series and side pockets affect investor NAV and incentive allocations?
questions.finding: Historical Irish/practitioner methods explain HWM equalization alternatives, but general side-pocket mechanics and private-partnership subscription entries are not fully resolved.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual side-pocket participation, dealing NAV, fee reversals, HWM, crystallization, and private-partnership subscription accounting depend on fund contracts and administrator records; the guide is historical Irish practice, not US authority.

questions.question: How do ASC 946 investor-class allocations reflect unrealized marks, carried interest and clawback at the reporting date?
questions.finding: ASC 946 fund-class allocation of marks, fees and carry is not the same reporting question as the GP/manager’s carry revenue or investment. The latter may involve Topic 606 or a fact-supported ownership model under interpretive sources.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual fund agreement, carry classification in GP/manager statements, clawback and participant compensation require entity-specific analysis and current GAAP review.

questions.question: How should ASC 946 subscription equalization and class capital transactions be reflected?
questions.finding: Hedge-fund share equalization must preserve each subscriber’s issue NAV/HWM and accrued-fee position, but these administrator methods do not answer the ASC 946 entry or private partnership subscription equalization amount.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual subscription ledger, LPA, administrator method, retroactive NAV adjustments and current ASC 946 treatment remain open.

recommended_additions: Add a focused ASC 946 fund financial-statement and close guide using KPMG’s current public technical handbook as interpretive context; clearly distinguish authority from professional interpretation.
Add a separate waterfall/carry schedule branch linked to a model LPA and actual fund-document inputs, plus a hedge classes/series/equalization/side-pocket branch using illustrative statements.
Retain the restricted IPEV lead as discovery-only pending a rights review; do not carry forward substantive claims.
Map fund, GP, manager and portfolio-company reporting as separate reporting entities.
Show the manager carry service-revenue versus ownership analysis and hedge equalization methods separately from ASC 946 fund-class entries.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
IPEV remains a rights-restricted discovery lead only; its substantive text is excluded and no valuation claim is based on it.
Current Codification wording and entity-specific application remain to be checked; this follow-up does not infer that current ASC verification requires paid access.
priority_rationale: Fund reporting crosses legal entities, NAV, investor capital, adviser fees and regulatory custody; available corpus routes are fragmented.

title: Forensic accounting and litigation support
baseline_summary: Baseline selects a fraud/control guide and audit, federal-control and household-employer questions. These provide partial adjacent coverage for financial-statement fraud, control design/operation and evidence; the named source population does not cover forensic engagement methodology, transaction tracing, litigation damages or federal expert testimony requirements.

questions.question: What work does forensic accounting commonly support across investigation, trial, and sentencing?
questions.finding: The prior DOJ practice article supports a bounded description of investigation, trial and sentencing work, including records analysis, tracing and loss/restition/forfeiture estimates.
questions.remaining_gap: General government-practice example only; not an engagement standard or a fact finding.

questions.question: What evidence and documentation supports a reproducible fraud trace?
questions.finding: NIST IR 8387 adds direct technical guidance on acquisition, preservation, provenance, chain-of-custody documentation, hashes, original and working copies, access and storage/transfer. Existing IRS bank-deposits guidance gives a separate example of testing non-income and duplicate-deposit explanations.
questions.remaining_gap: No general private forensic-accounting trace protocol was established; civil hold, custodian, platform and tribunal duties depend on the matter.

questions.question: How should fraud loss, damages or asset dissipation be quantified?
questions.finding: FJC Fourth Edition Guide to Economic Damages provides a nonbinding but-for comparison framework; lost-profit work requires evidence supporting counterfactual prices, units/market share and avoided costs.
questions.remaining_gap: Legal measure, causation, valuation date, mitigation and recoverability remain claim- and case-dependent; no universal damages formula.

questions.question: What supports expert opinions and disclosures in federal civil litigation?
questions.finding: Directly read Rule 702 in the official U.S. Courts Rules of Evidence compilation dated Dec. 1, 2024. The proponent must show more likely than not that testimony will help, is based on sufficient facts/data and reliable methods, and reliably applies them; prior direct Rule 26 read covers expert disclosures.
questions.remaining_gap: Verify current tribunal compilation, governing orders, state rules, case law, privilege and case facts.

questions.question: What professional standard applies to AICPA-member forensic services?
questions.finding: Prior direct read of public SSFS No. 1 supports a bounded standard for covered forensic services by AICPA members accepted on/after Jan. 1, 2020.
questions.remaining_gap: Confirm current text, member/service scope and later amendments; SSFS is not a universal legal requirement.

recommended_additions: Evidence intake and preservation guide linking original files, hashes, custody, source-to-ledger lineage, transformations, reconciliations and alternative explanations.
Damages and expert-report guide that records legal theory, but-for facts, valuation date, mitigation and recoverability without turning an economic reference guide into a universal legal formula.
unresolved_gaps: No general private forensic trace protocol was established; NIST is technical handler guidance and the IRS bank-deposits method is limited to criminal tax investigations.
No state/arbitration/criminal-procedure survey or empirical error-rate comparison was completed.
Actual preservation, causation, damages and admissibility depend on evidence, legal theory, tribunal, counsel and case orders.
priority_rationale: Audit-fraud coverage is materially adjacent but a person building a forensic agent needs distinct work products, evidence lineage, quantification assumptions and litigation constraints.

title: Bankruptcy and restructuring accounting
baseline_summary: Baseline selects subsequent-event/going-concern and IFRS restructuring/disposal questions, with historical US exit/discontinued-operation sources and an ASC landing page. It does not directly cover debtor operating reports, claim populations, ASC 852, or liquidation-basis accounting.

questions.question: Which Chapter 11 operating report and reporting period apply to this debtor?
questions.finding: UST distinguishes 11-MOR/11-PCR from Official Form 425C for small-business/Subchapter V before confirmation and directs the post-confirmation route to the district UST; usual monthly deadline is the 21st following month, subject to local directions.
questions.remaining_gap: Confirm debtor classification, case phase, current form version, district UST, local rules and orders.

questions.question: How should debtor statutory operating reports tie to books and supporting evidence?
questions.finding: Direct reading of the UST 11-MOR instructions adds book-to-report details: bank/investment cash totals, reconciliation and difference explanations, separated pre/postpetition obligations, cash receipts/disbursements, operations, and debtor-only centralized cash presentation.
questions.remaining_gap: Current version, district and court instructions determine the actual forms, attachments, accounts, basis and cutoff.

questions.question: How should debtor schedules and creditor claims be reconciled?
questions.finding: Rules 3001, 3003 and 3007 organize proof, Chapter 9/11 scheduled-claim treatment, case bar date and objections; 11 U.S.C. §§501-502 supply filing/allowance rules and §506(a) ties secured status to allowed-claim and collateral-value determinations.
questions.remaining_gap: General path is supported; actual allowance, validity, priority, secured amount, value, distribution and post-2024 statutory changes depend on current law and the docket.

questions.question: What current US GAAP governs Chapter 11 reorganization and fresh-start accounting?
questions.finding: The prior directly read EY April 2026 guide provides bounded fresh-start criteria and allocation overview. The Codification site returned no readable text in this access attempt; no current consolidated ASC 852 conclusion is claimed.
questions.remaining_gap: Current ASC 852 and related Topics, amendments, measurement/disclosure details and debtor plan/value facts remain unresolved; the access attempt is not evidence of a paywall.

questions.question: When does liquidation basis begin and how are assets/liabilities presented?
questions.finding: Directly reread public ASU 2013-07 amendment paragraphs on imminent liquidation, prospective transition, expected disposal proceeds, disposal costs, continued liabilities absent legal release and the two liquidation-basis statements.
questions.remaining_gap: Current consolidated ASC 205-30 amendments and full disclosure checklist remain unverified; distinguish current-GAAP application from the historical public ASU text.

recommended_additions: Chapter 11 debtor reporting guide with form-selection, due date, book-to-form, bank/investment reconciliation, pre/postpetition split, support and signoff.
Claims reconciliation guide that retains scheduled amount, proof, asserted status, §502 allowance, §506 valuation, objections and court outcome separately.
Separate current-authority review for ASC 852 and ASC 205-30, with EY/ASU references labeled as nonauthoritative interpretation/historical amendment.
unresolved_gaps: Current consolidated ASC 852 and ASC 205-30 were not directly read; the access attempt returned no readable text, which does not establish subscription or license status.
UST report instructions read are dated Dec. 7, 2022; current form, district UST, local orders and debtor classification can change exact routing.
Claims allowance, priority, lien validity, valuation, distribution and enactments after the 2024 U.S. Code edition require current rule/statute and docket review.
priority_rationale: Current baseline is centered on going concern and restructuring concepts, while bankruptcy creates distinct statutory reporting and claims populations and separate US GAAP models.

title: Employee benefit plan accounting
baseline_summary: Baseline contains employer-benefit and fringe-tax guidance, IAS 19, historical FAS 87 and DOL reporting/disclosure guidance. It does not directly address the plan as reporting entity, plan statements, Form 5500 schedules, plan assets/participant accounts or modern ERISA audit scope.

questions.question: How are employer accounting and plan accounting separated?
questions.finding: A direct IRS Form 5500 Corner reread and actual DB/DC plan statements reinforce that sponsor/employer accounting, plan financial statements and regulatory Form 5500 reporting are separate reporting roles.
questions.remaining_gap: Specific employer and plan entries depend on current standards, plan structure/documents and facts.

questions.question: What populations support plan financial statements and reporting?
questions.finding: IRS overview plus direct 2025 DOL instructions identify the Form 5500 reporting purpose, filer/form routes, Schedule H/I populations and filing-year branches.
questions.remaining_gap: Current plan GAAP recognition/presentation and exact schedule population still depend on ASC 960/962/965, plan type, year and plan facts.

questions.question: How are contributions, participant balances, investments and distributions evidenced?
questions.finding: Actual 2025 DC 11-K and DB statements provide source-backed examples of investment, receivable, participant loan, expense, contribution, benefit, rollforward and actuarial populations.
questions.remaining_gap: Examples do not establish current recognition, measurement, master-trust or participant-allocation rules; current plan GAAP remains unverified.

questions.question: When is a plan audit required and what can the audit address?
questions.finding: 2025 instructions add current-year schedule/audit and ERISA §103(a)(3)(C) election routing; current eCFR §2520.104-46 directly states qualifying small-pension waiver asset/bonding, disclosures and records conditions.
questions.remaining_gap: Plan classification, audit standard details, election prerequisites, current-year facts and distinct welfare/other exceptions still require review.

questions.question: What special requirements apply to a defined-benefit plan?
questions.finding: 2025 instructions route single-employer DB plans to Schedule SB and multiemployer DB plans to Schedule MB with enrolled-actuary certification; an actual audited DB example illustrates plan-related assets/liabilities and accumulated benefit information.
questions.remaining_gap: Current plan GAAP, actuarial measurement, minimum funding, PBGC coverage and sponsor accounting need separate authoritative and fact-specific review.

questions.question: How does the current Form 5500 small-plan count relate to an ERISA audit requirement or waiver?
questions.finding: 2025 instructions and current regulation confirm plan-year/type-specific count and filing routes and that the small pension audit waiver is a separate conditional branch; DC beginning-year account-balance count rule applies from plan years beginning Jan. 1, 2023.
questions.remaining_gap: Apply the current year, plan type, count, assets/bonding, disclosures and other filing exceptions to the actual plan.

recommended_additions: Separate sponsor accounting, plan financial statements, Form 5500 reporting and ERISA audit decision paths.
Plan close map from payroll and participant subledger to trust/custodian evidence, investments, benefits, fees, plan statements and Form 5500 schedules.
Current FASB plan-GAAP and AICPA audit-standard verification pointer; do not treat 2015 ASU or illustrative filings as complete current GAAP.
unresolved_gaps: Current consolidated ASC 960/962/965 requirements were not directly read; zero-text ASC attempt is not proof of paywall or unavailability.
Current audit-standard requirements and every ERISA §103(a)(3)(C) prerequisite were not fully reviewed.
Plan type, count, ERISA coverage, waiver conditions, trust/master trust, actuarial assumptions and other filing exceptions change the result.
priority_rationale: An employer benefit guide does not answer the separate reporting, participant-account, investment and ERISA filing questions of a plan administrator or plan auditor.

title: Small-business reporting and accountant services
baseline_summary: Baseline provides framework routing, special-purpose assurance and professional-governance coverage but is broad/global and not a practical US small-business basis-conversion or accountant-service distinction guide.

questions.question: How should cash, modified-cash, tax and US GAAP outputs be distinguished?
questions.finding: IRS tax cash/accrual and inventory rules are tax-method guidance; Deloitte explains special-purpose cash, modified-cash, tax, regulatory and contractual bases and notes there is no standardized modified-cash recipe.
questions.remaining_gap: Need the intended users, contract, included/excluded accruals and current SSARS/reporting rules to define the basis for the entity.

questions.question: What bookkeeping evidence supports a small-business close and financial reports?
questions.finding: Prior direct IRS Pub. 583 reading supports source documents, separate business banking, recordkeeping and bank reconciliation as useful tax-close evidence.
questions.remaining_gap: Retention and control requirements remain tax-, contract-, employment-, litigation- and entity-dependent.

questions.question: When can a taxpayer use cash vs accrual and change methods?
questions.finding: For covered §448(c) corporation/partnership tests, Rev. Proc. 2025-32 states a $32 million average gross-receipts threshold for tax years beginning in 2026; Pub. 334 describes cash/accrual, inventory exception and Form 3115 method changes.
questions.remaining_gap: The threshold is not universal cash-method permission; entity type, aggregated receipts, tax-shelter, inventory, contracts and tax year must be checked.

questions.question: What distinguishes preparation, compilation, review and audit engagements?
questions.finding: AICPA public comparison distinguishes no-assurance preparation/compilation, limited-assurance review and reasonable-assurance audit; SSARS 27 summary describes a narrow future-effective CS 100/AR-C 70 preparation exception.
questions.remaining_gap: Full current AR-C/AU-C text, exact report legends, prerequisites and state overlays remain unread; SSARS 27 was available here only as a public summary.

questions.question: What is the accountant’s responsibility boundary for the requested service?
questions.finding: Public AICPA service guidance supports stating the selected service and assurance boundary; SSARS 27 summary clarifies one narrow consulting-engagement exception.
questions.remaining_gap: Engagement letter, management responsibility, client records, independence, exact current standards, state law and actual service facts determine the accountant’s duties.

recommended_additions: Basis/service selector that distinguishes tax, internal, contractual/regulatory and GAAP reports and makes the assurance level and selected basis visible.
Tax-method route that collects year, entity, aggregation, tax-shelter, inventory, contract and method-change facts before showing a cash/accrual answer.
Close-evidence checklist tying source documents, bank reconciliation, ledger and report lines, with unsupported estimates flagged for review.
unresolved_gaps: Modified cash has no single standardized adjustment recipe in the sources reviewed.
Full current AR-C/AU-C text, exact report wording, engagement exclusions and state-law duties were not read; SSARS 27 source is summary only.
Tax-method eligibility depends on facts not supplied, and 2026 threshold does not create a universal cash-method right.
priority_rationale: Existing basis and assurance guides do not explain the common small-business gap between cash records, tax returns, adjusted statements and engagement assurance level.

title: Cost and managerial accounting
baseline_status: partial; existing inventory/allocation/planning/performance records supplemented with a dated professional normal-capacity and standard-cost interpretation, an ABC/standard costing practitioner discussion, and an original profitability decision example
baseline_summary: OpenStax gives educational method and variance mechanics; FAS 151 is historical; FAR 31 answers federal contract cost questions rather than external inventory accounting. New evidence adds KPMG October 2025 interpretive material on normal capacity and standard costs, an IMA 2020 ABC and standard-cost article, and a constructed avoidable-cost case.

questions.question: How should job, process, standard and activity-based methods select cost objects and drivers?
questions.finding: Educational job/process distinctions plus the IMA practitioner discussion support selecting a job, process, activity or hybrid cost object according to output homogeneity, resource consumption and the decision purpose. ABC causal drivers and routine standard rates can coexist; not every common cost must be allocated for every decision.
questions.remaining_gap: IMA evidence is dated and its current URL redirects; no current empirical study or entity data establishes the cost-benefit point for a particular system.

questions.question: How are variable and fixed production overhead treated, including normal capacity, idle capacity and abnormal waste?
questions.finding: KPMG October 2025 interprets variable overhead using actual facility use and fixed overhead using an entity-specific normal-capacity range; abnormally low capacity leaves unallocated overhead in expense, while abnormally high capacity reduces unit allocation. The guide includes a numerical example and distinguishes abnormal spoilage from expected process loss.
questions.remaining_gap: Current FASB paragraphs were not independently extracted in this session; actual normal capacity, consistent inventory policy, other industry rules and award-specific allowability remain to be verified.

questions.question: How should standard costs and variances be reconciled to actual cost?
questions.finding: KPMG quotes ASC 330-10-30-12: standards are acceptable when adjusted at reasonable intervals to approximate a recognized cost basis at the balance-sheet date. That supports a close reconciliation, but the variance report itself is not a prescribed journal entry. FAR 31.201-1 separately requires applicable variance adjustment for contract total cost.
questions.remaining_gap: No single variance allocation journal-entry convention or entity inventory adjustment method was established; GAAP inventory, managerial variance analysis and allowable contract cost remain separate.

questions.question: How should customer, product, service and segment profitability use allocations?
questions.finding: The IMA discussion supports using activity drivers when broad volume allocations obscure resource consumption. The supplement adds an original service-line example: a line with $20,000 fully allocated profit causes a $260,000 decrease in company operating income if closed, under stated assumptions, because it loses $380,000 contribution and saves only $120,000 avoidable fixed cost.
questions.remaining_gap: The example is illustrative, not an external reporting allocation rule; real decisions depend on demand transfer, capacity constraints, timing, avoidability and entity data.

recommended_additions: Verify exact current ASC 330 text and any relevant exceptions before writing external-reporting instructions.
If expanding decision-cost coverage, use a rights-cleared, dated source and entity-specific facts to illustrate demand transfer and capacity constraints.
unresolved_gaps: Current Codification paragraph page did not return extractable text in the research browser; no conclusion about payment or licensing access is drawn.
IMA source is a 2020 practitioner piece whose old URL now redirects; current practice support and source-reuse rights are unverified.
No empirical costing-system accuracy evidence or real entity cost ledger was reviewed.
priority_rationale: The main gap was the bridge between internal cost methods, external inventory cost and federal allowability. The new evidence answers general method and normal-capacity questions while preserving those three distinct measurement purposes.

title: Private equity, venture capital, and hedge funds
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 9 guide matches, 36 question matches, 19 assessment matches, and 54 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: How do PE/VC valuation and recent-round calibration support fair value by security class?
questions.finding: BDO’s 2018 working-draft interpretation expands the unit-of-account, calibration and model-selection map; current authoritative security-class guidance and any specific valuation remain unverified.
questions.remaining_gap: Current authoritative security-class/fair-value guidance remains unverified; the BDO source summarizes a 2018 working draft, and actual rights, inputs and valuation require case-specific analysis; IPEV remains excluded.

questions.question: How do calls, distributions, unfunded commitments and investor notices reconcile?
questions.finding: Prior ILPA and IRS materials already support call, distribution, unfunded-commitment and investor-notice reconciliation.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual LPA and unusual call/distribution rights remain untested.

questions.question: How are preferred return, catch-up, carry, escrow and clawback modeled?
questions.finding: Prior ILPA model LPA gives one preferred-return/catch-up/carry/clawback illustration; no new waterfall evidence was added.
questions.remaining_gap: Escrow, clawback security, whole-fund versus deal-by-deal waterfall and actual carry terms remain agreement-specific.

questions.question: How do fund and adviser reporting requirements differ after the 2023 rule vacatur?
questions.finding: Prior SEC vacatur and custody/Form PF sources remain the basis for the bounded fund/adviser regulatory distinction.
questions.remaining_gap: Recheck adviser-specific custody, filing thresholds, CFTC/ERISA status and rule changes for the relevant date.

questions.question: How should hedge fund dealing NAV, high-water marks, equalization and side pockets be computed?
questions.finding: Historical Irish administrator/practitioner materials describe investor capital accounts, series accounting and equalization methods each preserve HWM/cohort fee history differently. A historical 2009 Irish administrator guide gives a $1,000 credit example and the brief derives a labeled later-$107 comparison.
questions.remaining_gap: Method selection, actual dealing NAV, fee reversals, side-pocket participation, crystallization, and redemption terms require the actual fund documents and administrator records.

questions.question: What does a new JV recognize at formation, and what is distinct for venturer accounting?
questions.finding: Prior FASB joint-venture formation source supports the effective-date and formation-versus-venturer-accounting distinction.
questions.remaining_gap: Investor’s subsequent control/equity-method analysis remains separate and fact-dependent.

questions.question: How do fund NAV and investor capital allocations reflect unrealized marks, fees, carry and clawback under ASC 946?
questions.finding: The fund’s ASC 946 investor-class allocation of fair-value changes, expenses and carry must be kept separate from a GP/manager’s carried-interest reporting as service revenue or an ownership interest.
questions.remaining_gap: The actual agreement determines the class allocation and carry amount; precise current ASC 946 treatment and GP/manager method remain to verify.

questions.question: How should new subscriptions/redemptions and class/series equalization be tracked?
questions.finding: Series/equalization structures explain how a new subscription can avoid bearing pre-entry appreciation fees, but they do not prescribe the ASC 946 transaction entry for a private partnership.
questions.remaining_gap: New-subscription pricing, share/interest issuance, retrospective equalization and redemption rights depend on LPA/PPM and actual subledger; GAAP entry not established.

recommended_additions: Add separate PE/VC waterfall/carry and hedge class/series/equalization/side-pocket question paths, supported by model and illustrative materials but gated on actual LPA/PPM terms.

Use KPMG ASC 946 and hedge financial-statement examples as clearly attributed technical interpretations and examples; preserve security-level private valuation calibration as an open research question.
Do not reuse substantive IPEV content; retain only its restricted discovery status pending rights review.
Add a class-level private-investment valuation calibration worksheet tied to rights and measurement-date facts.
Compare equalization-credit/deposit, contingent-liquidation, investor-account and share-series methods; keep subscription and HWM terms explicit.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
IPEV valuation content remains restricted and is not used; private security calibration remains an open question.
Current Codification wording and entity-specific application remain to be checked; this follow-up does not infer that current ASC verification requires paid access.
priority_rationale: PE/VC/hedge fund allocation, valuation and performance fee mechanics have material investor-reporting consequences and are absent from current dedicated guides.

title: Real estate ownership and property management
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 4 guide matches, 21 question matches, 13 assessment matches, and 28 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: How should owner, developer, manager, broker, contractor and REIT roles route?
questions.finding: California provides a bounded role/accounting route when a licensed broker handles another person’s property-management funds: the broker must maintain trust-fund and separate beneficiary records and respect trust-fund deposit/disbursement rules. This does not define roles or law nationwide.
questions.remaining_gap: Owner/developer/manager/broker/contractor/REIT roles depend on entity chart, ownership, contracts, state licensing and law; the California broker rule does not cover every manager.

questions.question: How should acquisition and development costs, CIP, placed-in-service, depreciation, and sale be separated?
questions.finding: Prior EY/KPMG and IRS sources already address development cost capitalization, book/tax depreciation and disposal; this pass adds no new cost guidance.
questions.remaining_gap: Property-use facts, component costs, acquired operating property, tax depreciation and exact current GAAP application remain.

questions.question: How should rent, incentives, deposits, and lease components flow through a rent roll?
questions.finding: Secondary GAAP interpretation describes operating-lessor straight-line rent when collection is probable, variable rent on occurrence/collection as applicable, and separates refundable deposits, nonrefundable consideration and deposit retention; IRS Pub. 527 separately treats refundable deposits and advance rent for tax.
questions.remaining_gap: Lease incentives, components/CAM and actual deposit rights require lease/state law facts; tax timing differs from book treatment; exact current Codification application remains.

questions.question: How should CAM/tenant recoveries reconcile and present?
questions.finding: Prior Deloitte lessor-reimbursement/CAM sources already support the bounded accounting route.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual lease terms, expedients, expense true-ups and allocation remain unreviewed.

questions.question: How should property-manager cash collection and owner settlement reconcile?
questions.finding: California’s 2026 broker rules require receipt/disbursement control records, separate beneficiary/transaction ledgers, monthly ledger-to-control reconciliation and written consent for a disbursement that would create a trust-fund shortfall. This supplies a jurisdiction-specific custody-accounting floor. A separate owner statement/remittance formula remains contract-dependent; the proposed property settlement schedule is an editorial control.
questions.remaining_gap: The regulations do not establish a national rule or the contractual timing/calculation of owner remittances. Determine broker/license status, state/local law, agency and trust terms, owner approvals, fee rights, bank activity and tenant liabilities from the actual engagement.

questions.question: What current federal REIT qualification data is needed?
questions.finding: The inspected Code and 2025 IRS instructions provide a general REIT threshold checklist, but the question asks for current qualification data and full consolidation-through date, attribution/look-through, TRS and cure details remain open.
questions.remaining_gap: GovInfo display did not show its consolidation-through date; 2025 instructions are not 2026 instructions. Verify the year’s statute, regulations, attribution/look-through, TRS, cure and current return requirements before concluding qualification.

recommended_additions: Expand the US real-estate guide with current ASC 970 development cost, ASC 842/606 lessor/CAM, real-estate seller revenue, and property-manager fee examples from EY, KPMG and Deloitte.

Add an owner/developer/manager reconciliation workbook outline that separates lease revenue, service fees, deposits, CAM billings/true-ups, project costs, tax basis and REIT tests; label control recommendations as editorial.
Keep state/local tenant-protection and property-manager trust/custody obligations as jurisdiction-specific open branches.
Add a role/basis map and a rent-roll bridge separating GAAP rent, tax rent, recoveries, deposits and liabilities.
Add a suggested manager-to-owner settlement control and a current-year REIT test data request; label controls as editorial and test status as date-dependent.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
Current Codification wording and entity-specific application remain to be checked; this follow-up does not infer that current ASC verification requires paid access.
priority_rationale: Owners, developers, managers and REITs have different book/tax/legal bases; existing coverage is partial and includes historical accounting standards.

title: Government contractors
baseline_status: partial; project WIP, allocation, FAR, DCAA preaward and federal-award adjacent material supplemented with direct DCAA pamphlet and ICE reads and a Topic 606 contract-balance bridge
baseline_summary: FAR allowability, DoD system clauses and construction/WIP sources were already present. The previous package correctly marked DCAA pamphlet discovery as discovery-only based on access then available. The follow-up directly read DCAA Manual 7641.90 pp. 13-15, ICE v2.0.1h pp. 5-7 and the current ICE page; it adds 2025 Topic 606 interpretation on job-cost progress, contract balances and variable-consideration adjustments.

questions.question: Which contract-specific rules determine allowability, allocability and record support?
questions.finding: FAR Part 31 and the applicable DoD clause remain the source of binding duties when incorporated. The directly read DCAA pamphlet adds auditor-practice and recommended accounting-system controls: job/cost-object accumulation, GL reconciliation, consistent direct/indirect treatment, labor distribution and records.
questions.remaining_gap: Agency supplements, award clause vintage, CAS coverage and selected cost edge cases require application to the actual award and disclosed practices.

questions.question: How do provisional billing rates, final indirect rates and incurred-cost proposals reconcile?
questions.finding: Prior FAR evidence supports provisional billing rates, final annual rates and proposal timing; the ICE v2.0.1h manual was directly read for schedule relationships, and the live DCAA page lists a July 2026 Power Query v1.08 build and says either it or the 2019 VB build is acceptable.
questions.remaining_gap: The current v1.08 manual was not opened; the contractor’s clause, disclosed practice, rate schedules, submission contents and adequacy remain contract/entity-specific.

questions.question: What labor timekeeping records support direct labor and prevent inconsistent charging?
questions.finding: The directly read June 26, 2012 DCAA pamphlet pp. 13-15 covers daily employee entry by actual work objective, correction trails, uncompensated overtime, employee certification and labor distribution. Supervisor cosignature is called recommended. These are DCAA system/audit recommendations, not independent contract clauses; binding requirements depend on the actual FAR/DFARS/CAS/award terms.
questions.remaining_gap: This answers a general source gap but is not a universal procedure; manual version, labor transfers, leave, subcontractors, agency/award terms and current adequacy criteria remain to be checked.

questions.question: How do cost-reimbursement invoices differ from cost-based progress financing?
questions.finding: Existing sources distinguish allowable incurred-cost reimbursement with provisional rates/final settlement from financing under the particular progress-payment clause. No new source was needed for this already-supported general distinction.
questions.remaining_gap: Executed clause/alternate, contract type, agency supplement, financing terms and payment facts determine actual treatment.

questions.question: How do contract-cost accounts relate to GAAP WIP, revenue and contract balances?
questions.finding: The December 2025 Topic 606 example bridges contract/job cost to a cost-to-cost progress measure, excludes costs that would distort progress, and calculates revenue and recognized cost. KPMG also distinguishes conditional contract assets, unconditional receivables, contract liabilities, and says invoice issuance alone does not determine the right’s classification. A rate settlement may affect customer-contract transaction price and revenue if it changes that consideration, requiring separate Topic 606 analysis.
questions.remaining_gap: KPMG is nonauthoritative interpretation; an actual outcome requires award/customer terms, actual performance obligations, enforceable rights, rate settlement facts and current Codification verification.

recommended_additions: Read the current ICE v1.08 user manual if a concrete filing workflow depends on it.
When applying this guide, map the executed clauses and the contractor’s disclosed accounting practices before designing cost-object, labor, rate and billing controls.
unresolved_gaps: The 2012 DCAA pamphlet provides historical general guidance, not a universal or binding procedure.
Current ICE v1.08 manual was only identified on the live page and not read; DCAA adequacy checklist was not used.
Current ASC text was not independently verified. No actual award, rate filing, contract ledger or settlement was reviewed.
priority_rationale: The follow-up closes the earlier direct-read gap for a key timekeeping source and explains the conceptual break between federal cost billing and customer-contract revenue, without replacing award-specific review.

title: Auto and equipment dealerships
baseline_status: partial; auto and inventory/revenue references supplemented with a 2026 equipment-dealer 10-K, equipment lender collateral definitions, and two related SEC correspondence observations
baseline_summary: Existing Lithia, Deere and dealer-group filings supplied auto and manufacturer-side examples. New Titan Machinery FY2026 disclosure covers equipment inventory, trade-ins, floorplan, incentives, parts/service, rental and warranty; an Alta ABL contract supplies lender classifications; the August issuer response and November SEC staff follow-up provide context for a rent-to-sell/rent-to-rent cash-flow distinction and its limits.

questions.question: How should floorplan borrowing and manufacturer floorplan assistance be tracked and recognized?
questions.finding: Titan and Lithia describe issuer-specific manufacturer floorplan liabilities, assistance/incentives and unit-sale relationships; Alta’s response describes its fact-specific manufacturer floorplan cash-flow position. These sources identify what to reconcile but do not establish a universal debt, interest or assistance policy.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual facility and program agreements, who pays the manufacturer, sale/payoff triggers, credits, customer consideration and current GAAP application remain unreviewed.

questions.question: How are new and used vehicle/equipment inventory and trade-ins valued and cut off?
questions.finding: Titan reports equipment inventory at specific identification/lower of cost or NRV, trade-ins using expected resale less expected gross profit and reconditioning, and reconditioning WIP. Lithia reports vehicle-specific inventory cost and trade-ins at stand-alone selling price using third-party pricing. The lender agreement separately defines collateral eligibility and serial/lien/appraisal evidence.
questions.remaining_gap: These differing issuer judgments do not decide another dealer’s valuation method, title/control and payoff cutoff, obsolescence, reconditioning policy, contract rights or GAAP recognition.

questions.question: How should manufacturer holdback, sales incentives and co-op funds be classified?
questions.finding: Titan and Lithia describe selected dealer-side incentive and reimbursement programs as inventory/cost-of-sales or expense reductions. Deere supplies only manufacturer-side estimation evidence. The arrangement, unit/expense linkage, volume conditions, clawbacks and customer-payable terms drive classification.
questions.remaining_gap: Co-op, volume-based, conditional, clawback and customer rebate contracts were not examined; the dealer cannot adopt the manufacturer’s reported accounting automatically.

questions.question: How do manufacturer warranty claims differ from dealer-sold service contracts?
questions.finding: Titan describes OEM repair reimbursement, third-party protection offerings and equipment service/parts revenue; Lithia reports OEM warranty receivables and net agency accounting for certain third-party extended-service contracts. This separates several economic roles but remains issuer-specific.
questions.remaining_gap: Contract promises, principal-agent facts, denial/chargeback exposure, deferred amounts, claim evidence and current Topic 606/other guidance must be evaluated for the dealer and contract.

questions.question: How should service, parts, internal labor and departmental profitability be reported?
questions.finding: Titan reports some equipment service plus consumed parts over time and standalone parts at a point in time; Lithia provides auto aftersales examples. The Area 7 IMA/decision-cost work supports clear, purpose-specific drivers for management reporting but is not a dealer department manual or external-reporting rule.
questions.remaining_gap: No public dealer department-control/cost-allocation manual or tested service-bay, technician time, parts-transfer, warranty, rework and internal labor dataset was reviewed.

questions.question: How do auto dealer examples transfer to equipment dealerships?
questions.finding: Equipment dealer evidence now demonstrates which methods can be compared and which should not be copied: equipment serial inventory, reconditioning, rental/demo fleet, unit-linked manufacturer support and machinery service/warranty differ from Lithia auto examples. The direct comparison provides a general transfer boundary, not a shared industry accounting policy.
questions.remaining_gap: Entity-specific agreements, equipment rental patterns and other auto/equipment dealers remain untested; ASC guidance was not independently verified.

recommended_additions: For a real dealer close, connect each unit/VIN/serial to title/control, inventory or rental use, floorplan, programs, work orders, warranty claims and sale/return cutoff.
If adding operating procedure content, first access a rights-cleared dealer service-department manual and actual cost/control example.
unresolved_gaps: All SEC issuer policies are entity-specific, and the Alta staff-review letters are not accounting standards or SEC endorsements.
No dealer-specific departmental profitability/control guide was inspected.
Actual contracts, lien/title dates, OEM programs, customer terms and exact current Codification application remain out of scope.
priority_rationale: Dealership coverage was previously generic or auto-focused. Current equipment issuer evidence materially improves comparison of inventory, fleet, financing and service while leaving universal policy claims bounded.

title: HOAs and condominiums
baseline_status: partial; previously missing CIRA coverage now supplemented with current 2026 Florida condominium statutes while preserving unresolved and conflicting assessment-recognition interpretations
baseline_summary: Prior sources included a FASB CIRA agenda handout, public practitioner positions, Florida and California laws, and federal HOA tax sources. New 2026 Florida §§ 718.111, 718.112 and 718.301 add current legal records/reporting, reserve/special-assessment and developer-turnover requirements. They do not settle Topic 972/606 recognition or general HOA law.

questions.question: How are assessments recognized and presented under US GAAP/Topic 972?
questions.finding: The FASB 2024 handout lists assessment recognition as an unresolved stakeholder issue. DesRoches argues regular/replacement assessments may be recognized when assessed if board discretion remains; it describes a conflicting PPC Guide liability-until-maintenance-costs view secondhand. Current Florida legal assessment powers give relevant context but no universal recognition answer.
questions.remaining_gap: Current ASC 972/606 text, independent access to the PPC position, governing documents, enforceability, promises, assessment due dates, refunds/reallocation rights and jurisdiction-specific law remain necessary.

questions.question: How do operating and reserve fund cash, fund balances and legal restrictions differ?
questions.finding: HOACPA’s 2018 article interprets quoted Topic 972 fund presentation and replacement-cost charging. Current Florida § 718.111 requires separate reserve accounting and narrowly limits investment-only commingling of cash; § 718.112 adds legal reserve-use controls. These do not decide ASC net-asset/fund-balance labels or replace current ASC verification.
questions.remaining_gap: The specialist source is dated, current ASC paragraphs were not directly read, and legal controls differ across associations and jurisdictions.

questions.question: What reserve-study, replacement and annual reporting information is required?
questions.finding: Current 2026 Florida §§ 718.111 and 718.112 add directly read Florida condominium financial reporting tiers, reserve formula and structural integrity reserve study rules, use restrictions and selected special-assessment/voting conditions. California sources remain another state-specific example. These are planning/legal duties, not automatic GAAP liabilities.
questions.remaining_gap: The 2026 Florida statutes do not answer requirements for an HOA or another state; check entity coverage, amendments, thresholds and effective dates at the reporting date.

questions.question: How are special assessments and future major-repair projects accounted for?
questions.finding: FASB agenda material and practitioner sources continue to show competing assessment-liability views. Current Florida law clarifies selected reserve funding, owner vote, reserve use and nonemergency special-assessment notice requirements, but legal approval, project planning and funding do not settle GAAP revenue/liability recognition or project capitalization.
questions.remaining_gap: Current Topic 972/606 text, declaration and approval terms, member rights, purpose/reallocation/refund conditions, performance promises, project cutoff and capitalization facts remain unresolved.

questions.question: What records and financial reporting accompany developer transition?
questions.finding: Current Florida § 718.301 directly specifies delivery of financial/source records and property at turnover and an independent CPA audit using GAAP statements/GAAS for the incorporation-to-turnover period or since the latest annual audit where annual audits have been performed. It establishes an audit and evidence boundary, not an opening-balance conclusion.
questions.remaining_gap: No source prescribes an opening-balance reconciliation procedure; actual title, bank, reserve, assessment, debt, contract, asset and cutoff evidence remains necessary. The statute is Florida condominium law only.

questions.question: How does § 528 tax treatment differ from financial-statement accounting?
questions.finding: Prior IRS Form 1120-H and Publication 557 evidence keeps a § 528 election, exempt-function income and tax qualification separate from financial-statement assessment and reserve accounting. No new tax source was needed.
questions.remaining_gap: Tax year, eligibility, election, state tax and taxable-corporation alternatives depend on the association’s facts.

recommended_additions: Verify exact current ASC 972/606 text and independently examine the competing PPC position before writing recognition instructions.
Add HOA/Chapter 720 and other-state legal branches only when a concrete jurisdictional coverage need is selected.
If opening balances are to be operationalized, build a records-based reconciliation using actual association records rather than inferring balances from statute or turnover audit duties.
unresolved_gaps: No current Topic 972/606 paragraphs were independently verified; FASB asc.fasb.org page returned no extractable text in the research browser. No conclusion about payment or access rights is drawn.
PPC view remains secondhand via the DesRoches authors; its current version and language were not read.
Florida Chapter 718 is condominium-specific; no Chapter 720 or other-state statutory analysis was added.
No actual bylaws, assessments, reserve study, project invoices, financial statements or turnover records were examined.
priority_rationale: The follow-up adds current, directly read Florida legal facts without collapsing legal reserve controls into financial recognition, and explicitly preserves the real professional disagreement about CIRA assessment liabilities.

title: SaaS and subscription businesses
baseline_summary: Existing coverage includes provider/customer role boundaries, subscription timing, hosted implementation, principal-agent, future ASU 2025-06 timing, and synthetic provider/customer close examples. The baseline is not evidence of complete SaaS treatment.

questions.question: How does advance billing/cash differ from earned deferred subscription revenue, and how do customer credits/refunds change the close?
questions.finding: Current EY interpretation distinguishes advance contract liabilities, expected refunds, service-level concessions and material rights/options; usage of a future-service credit is not automatically revenue or a refund. Classification still depends on enforceable contract terms, usage/credit records and any remittance duty.
questions.remaining_gap: No actual credits, customer contract population, expected-refund estimate or unclaimed-property analysis was available. Current consolidated ASC text was not directly verified; the observed browser limitation is not evidence of paid-access necessity.

questions.question: How are SaaS contract modifications and blend-and-extend renewals accounted for?
questions.finding: Current EY interpretation updates the general framework: separate-contract treatment requires added distinct service priced at standalone selling price; otherwise assess remaining-service distinctness and apply prospective or catch-up accounting as indicated. A blended price alone does not decide the outcome.
questions.remaining_gap: No renewal or modification contract was tested, and the public firm guidance is not authoritative FASB text.

questions.question: When should usage-based fees be recognized, and how do credits/minimums/rollovers affect it?
questions.finding: Usage-fee guidance distinguishes period-specific allocation when usage pricing faithfully depicts service delivered from estimating variable consideration and recognizing it over the service period subject to constraint. Minimum commitments, tiers, unused credits and rollover rights require their contract terms and may implicate a material right or breakage.
questions.remaining_gap: No minimum/rollover agreement or live usage population was inspected; public interpretation does not choose entity-specific terms or resolve current consolidated Topic 606.

questions.question: Which sales commissions qualify for capitalization and how should renewal commissions be amortized?
questions.finding: No new evidence in this follow-up. The prior source-supported general rule remains: qualifying incremental costs of obtaining a contract are capitalized when recoverable, subject to the practical expedient; amortization follows related transfer of services.
questions.remaining_gap: Commission plan, renewal commensurateness, clawback terms, expected customer life and impairment remain entity-specific.

questions.question: How do provider development, customer's hosted implementation and internal-use software capitalization differ?
questions.finding: ASU 2025-06 retains management authorization/funding plus probable completion and intended use, and requires an assessment of significant development uncertainty. The probable threshold is not met until such uncertainty is resolved; examples include novel/unproven functionality not resolved by coding and testing, or significant performance requirements not identified or continuing to be substantially revised. The amendment is future-effective for most calendar-year entities absent early adoption.
questions.remaining_gap: Provider ASC 985-20 versus 350-40 classification, actual entity election/adoption and project evidence still require review; the ASU is issued update text, not the entire current Codification.

recommended_additions: Add separate workpaper populations for deferred subscription service, prepaid usage rights, concessions/refunds and breakage, with contract-specific flags for term, rollover, minimum, refundability, material right and unclaimed-property obligation.
Enrich provider software-cost coverage with ASC 985-20 technical-feasibility evidence and a hosted-only SaaS classification decision branch, labeling KPMG as interpretive rather than authoritative.
Add a workpaper connecting subscription contract/version, service period, usage events, billings/cash, contract liability, modification and commission assets.
unresolved_gaps: Current consolidated ASC 606/340-40 text, service-contract and IP license tests, and entity-specific policy/adoption.
No entity contract tested for usage credits, service-level credits, refunds, rollovers, minimums, renewal rights, or state unclaimed-property requirements.
Provider hosted-only software-cost classification under ASC 350-40 versus ASC 985-20 remains fact-specific despite new KPMG interpretive coverage.
Tax, state SaaS/digital sales tax, enforceability, and non-US VAT.
priority_rationale: SaaS revenue depends on contract/version/usage evidence and subscription providers often have material deferred balances and commission assets; filling the specific evidence gaps improves decision support without duplicating existing overview coverage.

title: E-commerce and marketplace sellers
baseline_summary: The existing trade guide and synthetic reconciliation already cover ownership, POS, returns, inventory, card clearing, settlement, and mutually exclusive marketplace principal/agent branches. The fixture excludes state sales tax and real platform evidence.

questions.question: How does a marketplace/processor settlement reconcile to sales, returns, tax, fees, reserves, receivables and bank cash?
questions.finding: Current Stripe report/API documentation supports a row-level reconciliation from balance activity through payout and bank, with source IDs, gross/fee/net, status, created/available dates and payout association. A labeled synthetic example ties to $8,985 available-funds payout under its stated assumptions; the $250 hold and $50 release transfer available/reserve balances and leave $200 held. IRS 1099-K gross information reporting is not the provider net settlement or GAAP revenue.
questions.remaining_gap: No actual account, statement, bank match, merchant terms, tax return or transaction population was available. Synthetic numbers are illustrative, not seller evidence; reserve presentation and tax/revenue treatment remain terms- and fact-dependent.

questions.question: How should post-sale returns, refunds, credits, chargebacks and dispute fees be distinguished?
questions.finding: Shopify documents that a refund may occur without a physical return and restocking is optional; Stripe distinguishes an issuer/network chargeback and balance debit from a seller refund. EY current interpretive guidance addresses refund liabilities and the separate recovery asset when expected inventory returns. The settlement event alone does not determine sale reversal, loss, fee, return or inventory recognition.
questions.remaining_gap: No seller/processor agreement, card-network rulebook, dispute case, return inspection or customer evidence was inspected; current Codification and entity policy need application.

questions.question: How should third-party fulfillment/custody, physical inventory and platform/storage/fulfillment fees be separated?
questions.finding: Amazon’s FBA inventory API identifies fulfillable, inbound, reserved, unfulfillable and researching populations, useful for status reconciliation. These fields do not establish title, existence, condition, valuation or cut-off. A dated AE/English contract was read only as a foreign comparator and is excluded from U.S. findings.
questions.remaining_gap: No U.S. seller agreement, actual FBA inventory response, 3PL confirmation, inventory ledger or physical count was inspected; ownership/control and fee accrual remain entity-specific.

questions.question: Which party collects/remits sales tax on marketplace sales and what reporting obligations remain?
questions.finding: The existing California facilitator source remains the only state-specific tax authority reviewed. The IRS 1099-K page adds the distinct federal gross-payment reporting rule but does not establish who must collect/remit state sales tax. Keep facilitator status and residual seller filing/record obligations separate from revenue and net settlements.
questions.remaining_gap: No national or 50-state review, current nexus thresholds or product taxability analysis was performed; governing jurisdiction and channel facts remain necessary.

questions.question: When is the seller/marketplace gross principal versus net agent?
questions.finding: No new evidence in this follow-up. The prior FASB source supports assessing control of each specified good/service before transfer; gross principal/net agent presentation does not follow from payout routing, tax facilitator role or fulfillment service alone.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual contract, specified promise, inventory/control facts and transfer terms were not available for an entity conclusion.

recommended_additions: Add source-backed settlement adapters for Shopify Payments, Amazon Flat File V2 and Stripe that map fields only to evidence populations, not presumed accounting entries.
Add a 3PL/FBA inventory tie-out with SKU/FNSKU mapping, inbound receipts, fulfillable/reserved/unfulfillable/researching, shipment/return/damage and physical-count differences.
Keep transaction recognition, principal-agent, return liability/recovery asset, processor fee, dispute loss and sales tax as separate accounting decision layers.
unresolved_gaps: Actual merchant statements/API responses, Amazon Inventory Ledger, 3PL confirmations and merchant contracts.
Chargeback/network rules and evidence for the status and accounting of each dispute.
Current state-by-state facilitator/nexus/product tax rules; California is sole jurisdiction read.
The new vendor docs specify workflow but do not settle GAAP treatment, inventory ownership, valuation or title.
priority_rationale: Existing corpus already has a strong merchant role and settlement fixture. Incremental work should target missing platform evidence and tax jurisdiction coverage rather than another generic retail example.

title: Oil and gas operators and nonoperators
baseline_summary: Existing corpus substantively separates operator, nonoperator, mineral royalty owner, contractor, purchaser settlement, ONRR reporting, dated SEC cost method, synthetic depletion, and historical ARO boundaries. The same current 2025 IRS partner K-1 instructions are also represented by corpus source src_family_office_irs_k1_1065_2025 (shared research key cp_irs_k1). It does not contain detailed current JIB procedure or legal title evidence.

questions.question: How should operator JIB chargeability and nonoperator review/audit connect to actual agreements and evidence?
questions.finding: NOG’s 2025 filing distinguishes its nonoperator role from operator advances expected to be applied to JIBs; SM Energy discloses receivables from co-owners for JIB charges. These actual filings improve the operator/nonoperator workpaper map, but neither establishes chargeability, overhead, audit timing or contractual rights under another party’s JOA. COPAS MFI-40 remains a July 2023 committee-approved draft without verified adoption.
questions.remaining_gap: No signed JOA/accounting procedure, final MFI-40, JIB invoice, underlying support or audit exception schedule was available. Contract chargeability and adjustment deadlines remain entity-dependent.

questions.question: How do purchaser sales, operator cash, revenue distributions, royalty and transport differ?
questions.finding: SM Energy’s 2025 revenue disclosure links production revenue to purchaser delivery/control and separately describes co-owner JIB receivables. Existing ONRR instructions separately identify federal/Indian royalty reporting and allowances. Together these support the general boundary among commodity sale, operator cash, co-owner cost recovery, royalty remittance and revenue presentation.
questions.remaining_gap: Purchaser agreements, title/transport terms, WI and net-revenue decks, private/state royalty terms and an actual settlement were not inspected.

questions.question: How do ownership changes affect billed costs, proceeds and mineral interests?
questions.finding: NOG public transaction filings show completed acquisition dates can differ from stated effective dates and separately identify a nonoperator WI versus the operator’s share. The Texas FAQ notes a payor may require a division order with effective date, decimal/type and other fields, but says it does not amend the JOA or lease and that the RRC lacks lease/royalty authority. These facts support separately dated ownership and payment decks, not a legal cutover conclusion.
questions.remaining_gap: No executed assignment, title opinion, lease, JOA, purchaser deck, division order or property ledger was inspected. RRC material is informal, Texas-specific and not title authority.

questions.question: Which financial reporting cost method, depletion and abandonment rules apply?
questions.finding: NOG’s 2025 10-K demonstrates a disclosed full-cost policy; SM Energy’s 2025 10-K demonstrates successful efforts. SM’s UOP denominator differs by pool: drilling/completion and field development costs use estimated net proved developed reserves, while proved leasehold costs use total net proved reserves. Existing dated SEC rules and IRS materials remain separate SEC-regulatory and federal tax references.
questions.remaining_gap: The examples do not select a reporting entity’s method or establish current consolidated SEC/ASC detail; its policy, eligibility, engineering reserve estimates, pool costs, ceiling/impairment and taxpayer basis/limits remain unverified.

questions.question: How are ARO and remediation distinguished, and how do GAAP, tax and royalty/regulatory amounts differ?
questions.finding: Current EY and Deloitte public interpretation distinguishes retirement-related legal ARO obligations from environmental remediation associated with improper operation/catastrophic events. NOG and SM Energy disclose current company-specific ARO policies and estimates. FAS 143 in the corpus is historical only, not current ASC.
questions.remaining_gap: No obligation instrument, current authoritative ASC text, asset-level ARO calculation, permit, state bond, tax return or remedial claim was reviewed. Scope, legal obligor, timing, rate and later estimate changes depend on facts and applicable law.

questions.question: Can ONRR royalty rate/allowance and gross transport amount be substituted with WI or division-order percentages?
questions.finding: Existing ONRR Release 4.5 keeps federal/Indian volume, value, payor, rate and transportation/processing allowances separate. The Texas FAQ’s limited division-order/payor decimal information adds one state-specific distinction. Neither ONRR rates/allowances nor a payee decimal substitutes for WI or GAAP revenue.
questions.remaining_gap: Only federal/Indian ONRR and a Texas FAQ were examined; private leases, other states, actual report months, well interests and legal rights require their own sources and facts.

recommended_additions: Add a JIB/nonoperator audit schedule keyed to the signed procedure, property, cost class, approval, overhead basis, adjustment window, support and ownership-effective date; treat MFI-40 only as an unverified proposal.
Add a separate federal tax depletion reference clearly marked taxpayer-level, with cost versus percentage depletion and entity/partner reporting distinction, not a GAAP calculation.
Maintain separately linked GAAP, tax, SEC, private royalty, ONRR and state-regulatory populations.
unresolved_gaps: Final/current COPAS interpretation and paid procedure details; MFI-40 adoption status is unverified.
Current ASC 932 and 410/450 full Codification plus entity-specific method/adoption.
JOA/lease/title/division order, state pooling and legal ownership facts.
Reserve engineering, GAAP depletion/full-cost ceiling, tax basis and tax eligibility. IRS source adds general federal tax distinctions only.
State severance tax, private royalty, plugging and environmental requirements.
priority_rationale: The corpus has a mature synthetic production/royalty/ARO boundary example; concrete operator/nonoperator JIB and effective-dated ownership procedures are the highest-value additions while preserving contractual, financial reporting, tax, and royalty bases as distinct.
